ORDER Heard on I.A. No.19643/2024, which is application for ignoring the defect/ dispensing with typed copy.
For the reasons mentioned in the application, I.A. No.19643/2024 is allowed and the defect is hereby ignored.

This is first bail application filed under section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of bail to the applicant, in connection with FIR/Crime No.249/2024 Date:-(Not mentioned) registered at P.S.- Anjad, District- Barwani (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under sections 363, 366, 376, 376 (2)(N) of the IPC and sections 3/4, 5/6 of the POCSO Act.
2. Prosecution story in brief is that, at the time of incident prosecutrix was minor around 16 years and 3 months and her lady friend/victim was also minor around 15 years and 8 months.
Prior to the incident prosecutrix knew NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35359 2 MCRC-52267-2024 the applicant.
Prosecutrix and applicant loved each other and applicant wanted to marry her.
On 27.04.2024 prosecutrix and her lady friend/victim left their home and went alongwith applicant to village Chaapri.
Applicant kept both prosecutrix and her lady friend/victim in a house.
On the next day lady friend of the prosecutrix returned from there.
Thereafter, applicant took the prosecutrix to Morbi, Gujarat and kept her alongwith him for 5 months.

sentences.text: She was recovered by the police on 26.04.2024.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has not committed the offence and has falsely been implicated in the case.
It is submitted that prosecutrix voluntarily left her house and went with the applicant.
It is also submitted that prosecutrix was a consenting party for sexual intercourse.
It is also submitted applicant has no criminal antecedents and he is in custody since 26.09.2024.
After completion of investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
Conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time for its disposal.
Under these circumstances, prayer is made for grant of bail to the applicant.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the prayer of the applicant and prayed for its rejection.

5. Having considered the submissions advanced from counsel for the parties, also considering the facts and circumstances, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Hence, the application is allowed.

6. It is directed that the applicant- VISHAL be released on bail upon NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:35359 3 MCRC-52267-2024

his/her furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his/her appearance before the trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the trial Court during pendency of the trial.
It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of section 480 (3) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
7. M.Cr.C. stands disposed of, accordingly.
C.c. as per rules.
(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE ajit Vishal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195388800/
